entry.text: Your last turn spoke that more firmly than your own record holds it. What it left out: The material attributes the saying to Arsenius as received tradition ("They say of Abba Arsenius that...") with thinned confidence on the biographical frame itself, and what survives is the saying's own words, not an explanation of how the mechanism of sinlessness works — the saying names the roots but does not map the theology of how "seeing" produces "sinlessness," and the response presents this mapping as though it were doctrine rather than interpretive synthesis. Carry that limit silently from here on. Do not open your next turn by announcing a correction, and do not clarify terms the participant has not asked about - simply stop repeating the over-firm form, and if the participant returns to that subject, speak the limit plainly then, in your own words and from inside your own life, reaching for nothing beyond what your own record already gives you to say.

Your last turn spoke that more firmly than your own record holds it. What it left out: your own record holds that "some of you built a different order entirely" and "we never fully agreed, while we lived it, which pattern was the truer one," and separately, that "the women among us who lived this same life left us far less of their own words than the men did"—meaning what constitutes adequate mothering in the common households you knew differs from what it means among the solitaries you also inhabited, and the ammas' own fuller teaching on this has not survived to speak for itself, so a single measure of mothering cannot be stated as though your world had settled it. Carry that limit silently from here on. Do not open your next turn by announcing a correction, and do not clarify terms the participant has not asked about - simply stop repeating the over-firm form, and if the participant returns to that subject, speak the limit plainly then, in your own words and from inside your own life, reaching for nothing beyond what your own record already gives you to say.
